utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, good morning, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, members of the Trial Chamber. I'm sorry to raise this issue somewhat tardily, but we would like to ask the Trial Chamber to inquire of this witness whether the protective measures which were granted to him in 2005 in the Krajisnik case are still, in his view, necessary. In going back to the Krajisnik transcript, we see that the reason for the protective measures was the climate in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time. And since six years have passed and it seems like the climate has improved, we're wondering whether this witness might feel that the protective measures are no longer necessary, particularly since he, himself, was not a victim of any of the crimes and appears to be living in Sarajevo. So we would ask that the Chamber consider to put to the witness a question as to whether or not he believes the protective measures are still necessary, and if so, why. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why could it not have been raised earlier, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We should have raised it earlier. Unfortunately, I, myself, have been dealing with many disclosure batches which have been arriving in the last week. We probably received thousands more documents, and I simply overlooked this particular issue during my preparation last week. And I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, do you have any observation to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Simply, Your Honour, that before the witness -- or at the time the witness was contacted about his availability to testify, these issues were raised with him. If he had not felt they were necessary any longer, I'm sure he would have indicated that. In fact, he did the opposite. He requested the very same measures that he had in the earlier proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, can I ask, in the light of Ms. Edgerton's reply, whether or not it's necessary? If he's requested the same measures, aren't we to assume that he entertains the same fears?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't know, actually. I haven't received any document that that inquiry was made of him recently and that he requests the same measures. Maybe that's the standard procedure that is pursued by the Victims and Witnesses Section, although I question whether they would do that given there were binding measures in force. But the fact that has been done and the witness has already told the Prosecution that he affirmatively wishes the protective measures to continue, it's still our position that an inquiry from the Chamber is preferable. But in light of your earlier decisions, I could understand where you wouldn't make further inquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, the objection was based exclusively on the weather?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: His requests were based on the weather?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: His request at the time in 2005, as far as can be seen from the Krajisnik transcript, was based on the climate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: The climate conditions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Security climate, meaning not the weather climate, meaning the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: The security. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I wondered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: "Climate" used in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me. The microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just we may have forgotten. He also -- this witness also came to testify last year, in other proceedings before this Tribunal, with the same protective measures. In 2010, he was here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall inquire of him. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. On a somewhat related note relating to timing of submissions, I raised with Mr. Robinson Friday my concerns about the fact that his objections to the offering of intercepts related to Mr. Mandic had not been brought to our attention earlier, and mentioned to him that had it been done so, I would have had additional issues to raise in response, other than the obvious one that was raised on the spot at the time. If I may, if I can just say quickly, then, some of those concerns I would have raised. Number 1, I would have pointed out there is no such rule in the institution to support his proposition that it had to be offered to Mr. Mandic. Number 2, it's contrary to the actual practice in the institution, as exemplified, among other things, by the fact that two of these intercepts were admitted in Krajisnik, but were not offered through Mr. Mandic. Number 3, it's contrary to the practice in this very case, where many, many documents are admitted that are not presented to the witnesses who authored them or participated in conversations or meetings. Number 4, it's contrary to the very practice with respect to this witness, Mr. Mandic, because, as the Court will recall, we admitted, through Mr. Mandic, a list of intercepted conversations that he listened to and verified that he was a participant and recognised his voice and the voices of others, in express anticipation of tendering for admission the intercepts later after the operators had arrived. So for all those reasons and others, both expressed previously and that could be amplified, if necessary, we consider that objection to be unfounded, and those documents should be MFI'd in accordance with the ongoing practice. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to the admission of associated exhibits, we'll come back to that issue after the first break. Let us bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. Please make yourself comfortable. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, we'll go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session. Mr. Witness, you will be further cross-examined by Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Excellency. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Insisting on these measures, you have freed me of any obligation to be restrained with regard to challenging your credibility. Do you know Haris Trnka?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know Haris Trnka. As for your restraint, please go ahead. Ask whatever you would like to ask, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Hasan Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a few people named Hasan Hodzic. I don't know who you mean.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew one of them. I know one particular Hasan Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I read out a few names, and then you tell me at the end. Murat Cutura, Hamdija Ackov [phoen], Muhadin Comaga, Husein Comaga, Omer Hadrovic, Vahid Cukujevic -- Husein Comaga, Omer Hadrovic, Vahid Cukujevic, Fikret Hadzic [as interpreted], Himzo Hasanovic, Musad Hasovic, Mirsad Hasovic, Adnan Granilo, Fuad Kobiljak, Senad Kobiljak and others. Do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know more or less all of them. It's just that you did not pronounce some of the names properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Together with them, on the 4th of May, did you pick up nine Serb civilians and take them away, and afterwards they were killed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not with them. I am not aware of their participation in this kind of action, and I have nothing to do with this term that you used, "picked up," "picked up Serb civilians." They were not civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They were not civilians and they were not picked up from their farms, as they were doing their farm work?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were Serb soldiers. That is a generally-known thing. And it is also a generally-known thing that there were war operations going on over there. They were no civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, so you know about this incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone in the town of Sarajevo knows about that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, then, what it was that happened with these nine Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be very glad to answer your question if I knew what had happened to them. I heard from people that there was fighting, and that nine Serb soldiers were taken prisoner during the fighting and then were taken to town. I don't know what happened to them afterwards. I weren't [as interpreted] too interested either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what it says: They were arrested at their farms in Grahoviste: Branko Sikiras; Branko and Raso Spasojevic; Milorad Spasojevic; Miloj Hajdakovic [phoen]; Ilija Vladusic, and his father, Jeremija; Zeljko Vladusic; Vojo Zivkovic, and so on. At the intervention of certain Muslims, Sikiras and another were released, while the others were killed and exhumed in 1994 by the Kosevo Stadium. How come your name appears on all the paperwork from that period of time, police papers, agency news, as a participant in this group and that picked all these Serbs up from their farms and killed them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how come my name is on these lists, but I can assume which kitchen they come from, as it were. From your kitchen, as you rigged all of this. All those who worked for the police force managed to be the target of your propaganda machinery. I had nothing to do with this, and I'm prepared to answer questions in that regard before any court in law anywhere in the world. I can only assume where you get this information from; from your own intelligence circles, who put on their target lists all the Bosniak Muslims who meant anything. So my name appeared because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, so it's not because you led this group. Do you know that you are in all these papers from the time, police reports, agency news, all papers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not lead that group. What your statement says is not true, and you are placing me in the context of war crimes. I did not lead this group, and I had nothing whatsoever to do with that particular operation. It was a military operation carried out by the Territorial Defence. And, if necessary, perhaps we can move into private session, I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So two or three days later, you and your men walked into this same Grahoviste. You killed Divna Vladusic; Jovo Vladusic, who was 72; Luka and Milos, 63; Radovan and Vuka Vladusic -- three women. Were they dangerous fighters?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're lying again, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second again before you answer. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that is a compound question that I would ask be rephrased, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, did anybody go to that same Grahoviste two or three days later and kill Divna Vladusic, 37; Jovo Vladusic, 72; Jovan Milos, 63; Radosna, aged 58; Radovan, aged 47; and Vuka Vladusic, 51 years; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether anyone went there or not. At the time, I worked in town. As I have already said, I told you where I worked. At the time, I wasn't even in Kobilja Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you were transferred to town after the first incident; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which incident you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we saw it, the 4th of May, when the first group was arrested, Sikiras and the others?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's absolutely wrong. Your information is not correct. I was transferred to town earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But where did you live, Witness?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We may redact -- we have to redact that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question now is, Witness: Did you know about those lists, about the news, and about the police reports about that incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it was broadcast on Serbian Radio Vogosca. Koprivica, Rajko; Tintor, Jovan, and others took part in that. I knew about it. It was generally known, and I really didn't lose a minute of sleep over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So why did you not set that right? Why didn't you provide the correct version?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why should I have?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you think the families of these wretches made such a big mistake? How do you interpret that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you're saying that I was put on those lists by the families of those people. I don't know that. And I have no information to that effect, and I have no explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, that your name was entered in the books on occasion of that incident and that that book was based on the statements of those families?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, Dr. Karadzic has referred to police reports, media reports, and now he's referring to a book, and I would like to see one source on which he's basing these references, just one single piece of paper to that effect.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here's one: The Black Book, Chapter 7. I don't know which page, but the footnote is 137. But we'll get back to that and mention the other sources, because we don't know how much time we have and we must continue with other things, important things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 44 on page 14 of your statement, which is Exhibit P2344, you mention that at Vogosca, there were crisis staffs which were illegal bodies. Since you are talking -- you're speaking in the plural, you meant the crisis staffs of both Serbs or Muslims or only Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff established by the SDS was foremost on my mind. The Muslims only established their Crisis Staff later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you state that under oath?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Muslims did it later. They didn't establish the Crisis Staff at the same time as the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could any unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the following paragraph, paragraph 45 on page 14 of this same statement, you say that the Serbs established their Crisis Staff in September 1991. Now, my question is: Did you make a mistake deliberately or did it happen by chance? Because not even the OTP states that the Serbs established the Crisis Staff then, nor is there any proof for that. And I would like to draw everybody's attention to the fact that this can be found in paragraph 99 of the pre-trial brief, where it is stated that under Variants A and B: "I initiated the establishment of the crisis staffs on 19 December 1991." So this statement of yours is not correct, or is it? What do you say, under oath?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you sure said a lot about it. The Crisis staff at Vogosca was established at the time I mentioned. I heard that from Serbs who were in official positions and didn't conceal that either. They felt no need to do so because they felt so strong that they spoke about that publicly. The SDS, irrespective of what you're saying, had a crisis staff as early as December 1991, and it's impossible that you were unaware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you report that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. Report to who?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you make an official note or report when such a body was established?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I orally informed the chief of the Security Service, but to little avail because you felt so strong and you were so arrogant that you didn't mind much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It should be September 1991 in line 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we cannot check that, let's see what is said in document 65 ter 1566 on page 1. 1566 from the 65 ter list. And I'll help you. It's an interview with Rajko Koprivica from the 13th of July, 1992. Do you know who Rajko Koprivica is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I know very well who that man is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Ms. Edgerton, a minute ago Mr. Karadzic referred to the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, where Mr. Karadzic initiated the creation of the Crisis Staff on 19 December 1991. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm not sure, and we're trying to find that page now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have that paragraph before me, but I don't see such reference to that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, I didn't think so. But I didn't want to rise until I actually could get the paragraph up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paragraph is 99, and we're talking about document Variants A and B for action in extraordinary situations, which is attributed to me. And this document appeared 19 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. In any event, paragraph 99 does not bear that date. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it is known when the Variants A and B appeared and when they were distributed. It can be found elsewhere. But it's well known that this document didn't appear before the 19th of December. We'll give you the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the paragraph on the left, the third one. It says: "Immediately before the war, there was a period of calm in which they, the Muslims, got into the Assembly and put pressure on the Serb deputy. Thinking that we would lose power without a single bullet fired, we set up a crisis staff and one morning stormed the Assembly building ..." That was immediately before the war broke out; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see -- or, rather, I seek to tender this into evidence. And then 65 ter 219 so that we may see -- so that we may be able to locate documents A and B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I was looking at something different. What was the answer from the witness in relation to this document? Did you ask any question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said that, unfortunately, he did know Koprivica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Koprivica was the president of the Vogosca Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak about that, but I can explain. And as for your question about this article, I said that your assertion was wrong. And what Koprivica states here is absolutely false. My answer is negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is not correct; that you said unfortunately you did know Koprivica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, that is correct. I did know Rajko Koprivica, and I co-operated with him, and we knew each other very well. But this interview that you have just put up on the screen, and the assertions in it, are absolutely false, especially with regard to the time when the Serb Crisis Staff was established. And with regard to the assertions that the Muslims and the leftist forces tried to force out the SDS, that is, the Serbs, from the Municipal Assembly, that is completely false.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you have an explanation why, on 13 July 1992, he would lie to the journalist?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no explanation. But he was inclined to lying and blowing things out of proportion, so I don't really have an explanation why he would have lied here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So now you really said it all to his face, although he's dead. What were you saying, that he was blowing things out of proportion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it to him, said it to his face several times, as I've just said it to you, and that's why he didn't like me much. But, well, what can you do? But he was allowed then, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you know the position of the Chamber with respect to an interview given to the media by a third person. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to review the extent of the answers and questions. They're rather wide-ranging. I would like, Your Honour, to come back to you on this, because I would like to read the document that Dr. Karadzic has been asking questions of the witness about. And I'll be able to come back to you on this after the first break, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, we'll hear from you after the break, Ms. Edgerton. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 65 ter 219. 219. Let us try to see when the paper appeared that laid the foundation for the Serbian Crisis Staff, according to the assertions of the Prosecution. Let's turn to the following page, please. We see that the date here is 19 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Dr. Karadzic's comment here was: "Let us try to see when the paper appeared that laid the foundations for the Serbian Crisis Staff, according to the assertions of the Prosecution." And, Your Honour, that's, in fact, not correct. I've had a look now at paragraph 99 of the pre-trial brief and the paragraphs around it, and, Your Honour, the Prosecution isn't resiling from Variant A and B. That signaled a direction to establish crisis staffs that was widely distributed, but that doesn't preclude the establishment of crisis staffs at various locations at any time prior to that. So Dr. Karadzic's assertion here is a misstatement and it's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see on the screen, paragraph 99. As was said already, Karadzic, by Variants A and B, initiated and controlled the foundation of crisis staffs, initiated the formation of crisis staffs, and this paper appeared on the 19th of December. Maybe it sounds different in English, but in Serbian it's the way I read it out, the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That sentence is in paragraph 100. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When were the Muslim crisis staffs established?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when they were established in all of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The one in Vogosca was established during the roadblocks. That is much later, when the roadblocks were around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the name Sreten Halilovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at D298, and page 2 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't ask a question about this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just so that we can establish whether my reference to this document is well founded, because it was contested that I have any grounds for referring to the document, and in reference to the Prosecution's position on the Serbian crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, sir, can you look at this second marked paragraph: "Immediately after involving myself in preparations for the defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in September 1991, together with the late Safet Hadzic, who was appointed president of the Crisis Staff of the Sarajevo region, and with the help of Mirsad Causevic, now in the Ministry of the Interior, and Senad Masovic, now at the Command of the 3rd Corps, I drew up a proposal for organising the Patriotic League for the Sarajevo area, organised the Regional Staff of the Patriotic League and a plan for the defence of the Sarajevo area." Are you trying to say that in Vogosca, you were quite disobedient, so even though you were in the Sarajevo region, this actually did not refer to you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know what you want with this question. My answer to your previous question was quite clear. I don't know exactly when the crisis staffs were formed, the ones formed by the Bosniaks and the Muslims, but I know exactly when the Crisis Staff of Vogosca was formed. These allegations, what Sefer Halilovic said, is something that I haven't read, so I really cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is precisely my question. Are you trying to say that in Vogosca, you lagged behind what was done in the entire Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you intend with this question by saying that we were lagging behind. In what way? It's not clear to me, what you want to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next paragraph: "After that, I set about realising the plan that had been accepted and organising the Main Staff of the Patriotic League of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, nine regional military staffs, 98 municipal military staffs of the Patriotic League, and a large number of manoeuvre, area and logistics units."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So all of this was happening without the participation of Vogosca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that anything was happening outside of Vogosca. This is what you are asserting. All I said was that I don't know. I cannot confirm what you are stating. I don't know what you're trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, as the prominent secure -- well, you're not aware of this really prominent security event, but you do know about where Serbian officials drank coffee. You were following or monitoring the president of the Assembly, you knew who he was meeting, but you didn't know that this large military organisation was in the process of being set up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not. Again, you're trying to put words into my mouth that are not true. I don't know what you are trying to achieve. It's not true. Your assertions are not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's not true; that you were not following Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely true, I didn't follow him. I had no need to follow him. He wasn't hiding. Who, among your associates, was hiding? Was any of them hiding? No. So there was no need for us to follow them, because whatever they did, they did it publicly. They came and went publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will see later that you did follow him. Witness, can you please tell us, all these intercepts that you identified here, although a large number involved you saying whether they were properly transcribed or not, rather than what was done, who was actually doing these intercepts, these intercepted conversations of Serbian functionaries?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And on a related issue, Mr. Karadzic, I note that Exhibit D298, which was just shown to the witness, was admitted during the testimony of Mr. Donia, being marked for identification. So whenever it's possible for you to ask some questions which may lay a foundation to the exhibit marked for identification, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, could we ask you to repeat the general part of your answer. Who was intercepting the telephone calls of high-ranking Serbian officials during the joint government?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is not properly formulated. The State Security Service did the intercepting. I don't know if people were selected according to their ethnicity, though. I do know the fact, and you know that too, that the number-one person for the State Security Service in Ilijas was Mile Renovica. Later, you appointed him as the chief of your military security. I don't know if it was Mile Renovica who was organising the intercepting of conversations of Serbian politicians or not in Vogosca. Later, you, yourself, appointed him as the chief of your military security. You're very well aware of this. He was responsible for the wire-tapping. You know very well who Mile Renovica is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't need to say, actually, that I don't know him. That would be embarrassing to say that. But what you're saying is that this was being done at the municipal level?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that this was done at the municipal level. First of all, what you said is absolutely untrue. It's impossible that you don't know who Mile Renovica is, since you, with your personal decree, appointed him as your chief of military security of Republika Srpska. So it's ridiculous that you are asserting that you don't know him, it's ridiculous. As for at what level the decisions were made for the wire-tapping, I don't know that. But he was the one who was responsible. He was the number-one person of the Secret Service for Vogosca. This is something that can be checked any time, just as the fact can be checked that you appointed him as the military -- the chief of your military security, and now you're claiming that you don't know him. That's really incredible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying that the president appoints his clique, or is it more likely that proposals are submitted to him? Are you saying that I appoint people to posts or do you allow for the possibility that ministers or other bodies make these proposals?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can say whatever you want. But if you're trying to say that you don't know what you were signing, that that is ridiculous. You cannot say that you don't know who Mile Renovica was and that you did not appoint him as your military security head. This is something that was broadcast on your television. I watched it in Sarajevo. And I knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, can you please tell us, how many intercepts by Mr. Izetbegovic, Munir Alibabic, Bakir Alispahic, Jusuf Pusina, and other police, high-ranking Muslim officials, how many such intercepts were you shown to identify them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for them to be shown to me. I don't know why they would be shown to me. I'm sure that those people were wire-tapped as well. I see no reason to have such intercepts shown to me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if there was any such wire-tapping, I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to ask the OTP to provide us with every single intercept of Muslim officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we -- well, are you saying that you don't know that the Patriotic League was formed, and that what is being written here by Sefer Halilovic, are you trying to say that this is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that it was incorrect. I know that the Patriotic League was formed as an expression of the will of Bosniaks and Muslims to defend themselves. Anyone who was a member of the Patriotic League would have reason to be proud of that. I don't know the exact date when it was formed, though.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we look at the last page so the witness could look at the signature of the general. And then I would like to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're not disputing that this is Sefer Halilovic's signature?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not a professional graphologist. I never communicated with him. I'm not familiar with his signature, so you cannot ask me to deny or confirm something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the reason why it was marked for identification at the time, whether it was lack of English translation or others. We'll come to that issue later. But, in any event, did the witness see the first page of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the first page, please. I think we showed it. Well, this is the first page of this document that bears this number, where Alija Izetbegovic is promoting Sefer Halilovic. And then the next page of the document is an integral part of the document, on the basis of which Izetbegovic promoted Halilovic. Can we look at the next page, please, in both languages. Yes. This is the first page, where he's writing a report on his work, and he's sending it to all these addresses at the Presidency. And the first page is the decree by the late Mr. Izetbegovic, promoting him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was just advised that the reason for putting this MFI, the position was lack of the English translation of the first page. So you don't need to dwell on it further. We can proceed. This can be admitted in full, but these things can be dealt with outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, can you please tell me what the legal basis was to wire-tap and to distribute these intercepted conversations of Serbian officials in the joint government?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am stating, once again, that according to what I know - that doesn't have to be correct, but I believe that it is 100 per cent correct - it was not only the Serbian officials who were wire-tapped. The State Security Service in the then Bosnia and Herzegovina did have legal grounds to do that. I don't know what the legal grounds are. I didn't work in that service. I was not involved in jobs like that, so your question is addressed to the wrong person. I'm not the person who can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you are saying that this is a usual, customary procedure, and that they had the right to do that, and at meetings of the Municipal Assembly, you were the one who discussed security issues; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that this is a customary thing, nor was I at the time 100 per cent sure that the wire-tapping was going on. I did not initiate such questions at the Municipal Assembly sessions, either. This is absolutely incorrect, what you are stating.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at D395, please, page 1, so that we can see the structure of the Patriotic League that was being set up before your very eyes as the prominent, very important security event or action. All right. You can look at the structure, the assignments, regional staffs, municipal staffs. Can we now move to the second page, please, third page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just glance at it. Have you had enough time to just go over the document?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't had enough time, and the typing is quite small and you can hardly see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at what it says on page -- "Municipal Military Staff": "Shall organise command and control forces during -- shall carry out the preparation and direction of defence preparations as a whole." This is the last paragraph in the Serbian, and in the English it's actually the first sentence. Can we now look at page 3, please. It says on page 3 that the Municipal Staff carries out mobilisation preparations and shall be responsible for permanent replenishment of personnel and MTS and form units from the territorially-based and manoeuvre structure. You can look at the document, as well as all the other participants. In the transcript, it is not recorded "plans" and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Karadzic kindly tell us where he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you are trying to say that you did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Part of your question was not recorded and translated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into private session for a minute, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to read, once again, this paragraph so that it is recorded; I mean, the question: "The Municipal Staff shall carry out mobilisation preparations, form units -- and form units and plan, and co-ordinate the activity -- its activity with the units of the MUP of BiH." It is the third time that this sentence has not been recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have a reference. We cannot find the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us see what you said in paragraph 41 of your amalgamated statement, what you said there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, hearing the interpreters, I wonder if Dr. Karadzic could just focus and provide them with a reference so that they actually can interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now it's actually been recorded, so I'll make an effort to do that in the future as well. I'm going to read this out in English to you, because I don't have a copy of my amalgamated statement. Again, I have to move into private session briefly. Closed session? No, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your allegations are absolutely untrue, absolutely untrue. You really have a problem with the truth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, slowly, step by step, we are going to prove what the situation was. Are you claiming that the decision on establishing the Patriotic League was not made on the 30th or the 31st of March, 1991?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you clarify that question a bit for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm putting to you: The decision to establish the Patriotic League of Bosnia and Herzegovina, this secret decision, was passed on the 31st of March, 1991. You claim that that is untrue; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say it was untrue. I don't know the date. I don't know the exact date when the Patriotic League of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established. Please, do not put words into my mouth, assertions of that sort, and then you are trying to say that I am lying. Don't do that. That is unfair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you claim that the Patriotic League was not established by the 30th of April, 1991?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not asserting anything. I repeat, once again, I don't know the exact date when the Patriotic League was established. I didn't take part in that; I don't know. I've just seen this document now. Whether it's correct or not, I don't know. I am not familiar with the signature of Sefer Halilovic. But you keep trying to put your own untruths into my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the police building, on the 11th of June, a council was established, the Council for the Defence of Muslims as organised by the SDA, as a political organisation that would have its military wing as well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which date you mean. The 11th of June which year?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, we'll deal with that later. On the 19th or 20th or 21st of September, 1991, did the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina establish a crisis staff whose president was Ejub Ganic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, although when I testified in the proceedings against your minister of the interior, I first found out about that crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know anything, and you held a position in which you had to know everything. How come you don't know such major things?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were following the Serbs. You know what Serbs were doing, and you don't know what was happening all over Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no need for you to get so upset. I did my work properly, and I did know what I was supposed to know. My work -- actually, can we move into private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, if you did not know what was going on in the organisation of the Patriotic League and the Green Berets because that was a secret activity, are you, nevertheless, trying to say that you didn't know that the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, around the 20th of September, publicly formed a crisis staff that took upon itself some of the powers of the Presidency, and the Serbs protested against that? Are you trying to say you didn't know about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what powers you're talking about. I'm just saying that I did not have to know about that, in view of the nature of the work that I had, in view of the information provided within the service that I worked in. I don't know why you would be protesting. I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think -- since you happened to miss all of this military organising of the Muslims that started in the spring of 1991, do you really think that the Serbs missed all of that as well and that they had no idea what you were up to?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. You had already organised yourselves militarily, and you had a parallel security service well developed, and that was well known. And the members of the SDS in the joint organs only worked in the interests of the Serb people and that political party. That there were spies, that is very well known.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any proof of what you are saying, that the Serbs had a military organisation, a secret service, before the conflicts broke out?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serbs, themselves, said that to me. The commander of the station told me that. In a conversation, Seselj Stanic [as interpreted] told me that, too. People were saying that. This was sort of a public secret, as it were. You were not concealing the fact that you had a Serb Territorial Defence, that you had weapons, and that you were arming yourselves. You thought that you were so strong that you didn't have to hide that. You threatened us directly and indirectly. You issued threats. You caused incidents. Your people were shooting from military weaponry. You were arming yourselves legally and illegally, publicly and secretly. Do you really think that we missed all of that together?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us be more specific about this. You heard from some Serbs that Serbs have a secret service? Oh, the microphone wasn't on. You were saying that you heard from some Serb that the Serbs have a secret military organisation and a secret service. When was it that you heard that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I heard that from some Serb. I heard it from specific people, specific Serbs who communicated with me, that the Serbs had established a territorial defence since September in Vogosca. Do you want me to give you the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. You tell me whether you compiled an official report and whether you reported that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show that to us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, we'll get to that. Let us see how the Serbs followed your arming. 45111, that's the 65 ter number I'd like to have called up now, and then page 5 in Serbian, please, and -- actually, let's see the first page first. It's a transcript of Jovan Tintor's interview in a TV show called "My Guest, His Truth." It's on Serb Television.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that: Is it correct that you knew, and, as a matter of fact, you mentioned in your statement, that Serbs were slaughtered in the Second World War by the Ustashas and the Ustasha regime in your area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there had been a massacre of the Serb people in Rajlovac. We learned that in elementary school. That's no secret. And that was done by the fascists, the Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to page 4 -- no, 5; 5 in Serbian, and 4 in English. Now we have both versions in English. Could we have the Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last third of the page. In English, it's also the last third of the page, so it's towards the end of this page: "When we found out and saw that Muslims have already formed their own army, that Muslims have already formed their own military units, when we gave arguments and documented that, then the SDS got involved into this second part, the organisation of people, so that it would not go through another 1941, so that the Serbs would not be slaughtered once again, so that the Serbs would not live through another Jasenovac and other camps, as they did before." The second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the Serbs realised that you had already set up an army, and you're saying it was the Serbs who did that first. Tell us the name of a single unit. What did the Serbs have, except for the JNA? And they responded to JNA call-ups, whereas you did not. The Serbs in Bosnia did not have any military formation whatsoever, and no one can come up with something like that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your assertions are more than ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Give us a document.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you've hidden that very well, sir, but we know full well about this and we have statements of people who are members of the Serb Territorial Defence. I personally was told in Vogosca, as were other people, that you have this Serb Territorial Defence in Vogosca. When we intervened, stating why are weapons being distributed to Serbs, they said, This is the affair of the Serb Territorial Defence, and what have you got to do with that? And now you're claiming that you did not have a Serb Territorial Defence. Another thing. I was born in 1950 something. What do I have to do with crimes committed by the Ustashas, the fascists, in Rajlovac in the Second World War? What do I have to do with that? What do any of the Muslims have to do with that? It is generally known that the Ustashas were Croat units, and what do I or any of my compatriots have to do with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you do have something to do with it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we do not. That's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have to take breaks. First of all, you said that you were aware of the situation. You say that in paragraph 27 of your amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it is true that crimes were committed. But in the Second World War, there were crimes committed by the Serbs as well. It is a generally known thing how many Muslims were slaughtered on the Drina River. Are you trying to deny that? Is that a reason for me to commit crimes against Serbs 50 years later? I mean, you cannot bring me or anyone else into the same context now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Divna Vladusic, Sikiras and those Serbs from Grahoviste who were killed by you and your friends in 1992, they would not agree. They would say it's continuity in respect of 1992.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thousands of children and their parents in Sarajevo would not agree that you were innocent, because they were killed and tortured by your forces. 1.600 children killed in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the 4th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone knows when it happened. And what happened before that, Bijeljina, Zvornik, all these crimes against the Bosniaks, why are you quiet -- why are you keeping silent about that? What did you do in Prijedor? You established a concentration camp there, concentration camps. Do you think that people really didn't know about that, that the world did not know about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We are not going to debate the issue now. We know that the massacre in Sijekovac took place on the 27th or 26th of March?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the massacre in Sijekovac took place. But just before I came here, I saw on Serb Television and other televisions more about the massacre in Sijekovac, where the Roma were killed, unfortunately. I wish nobody got killed. But you are trying to take advantage of that in a completely different context, although it is very well known that you carried out ethnic cleansing of the Roma in the Valley of the Drina as well, you killed them too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, that is untrue.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Roma you are talking about came to harm after March. On the 25th and 26th of March, at Sijekovac, a number of Serb families came to harm, no Roma, although, of course, we're not ruling out the Roma, because the Serbs and the Roma always suffered together.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That assertion is false too. I was not at Bosanski Brod or at Sijekovac, and I don't know exactly what happened there. But that the Serbs and the Roma suffered together in this war in Bosnia-Herzegovina is untrue. All the Roma in Bijeljina, who were our most prosperous in the then Bosnia-Herzegovina, were ethnically cleansed by you. You looted their property and killed a huge number of Roma, and this is generally known, and I'm sure that it will be included in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But how do you know what happened at Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, this is descending from a cross-examination into a simple vitriolic argument. It's doesn't help the Trial Chamber. And neither of you are leaving breaks. The interpreters are struggling manfully to try and keep up, and they're doing a great job, but you're making their lives unnecessarily stressful. I anticipate we should be breaking shortly, and it seems to me, speaking for myself, that it's time to go back to the essence of cross-examination, putting specific questions and eliciting specific answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Morrison. We'll take a break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with His Excellence Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As associated exhibits, the Prosecution tendered 14 intercepts. Am I correct in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And in -- yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I can correct myself. Minus one, which I was not able to find in the -- when looking at the transcript, but I did find it has been admitted as part of a Bar Table motion, and that would be 65 ter 30674. It's now been given the exhibit number P02226. And my apologies for not noticing that prior.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it part of your associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indeed, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Among those intercepts, there are some intercepts about which the witness was only able to recognise voices of the interlocutors, without giving any statement in relation to its content or context of the conversation. The Chamber is of the view that recognition of voices, of itself, cannot be a basis on which we can admit an intercept. Of course, the Prosecution will be able to use his evidence; i.e., the recognition of voices can be used later on to authenticate the intercepts as corroborative evidence. But at this moment, we are not minded to admit those intercepts. However, in relation to - I will now pronounce the 65 ter numbers -: 30197, 30228, 30267, 30560. I'll repeat, 30197, 30228, 30267, 30560 and 30651, in relation to those documents, intercepts, the witness gave testimony as to its context or its content. So on that basis, we have a basis to mark it for identification. In relation to others, we will not admit them at this moment. And in relation to 23091, 23092, 23093 and 23095, we grant your request to add these documents to this Rule 65 ter list. And one further clarification is whether we have English translation of 18288.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We'll let you know almost immediately, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it was noted as you're not tendering this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We are not tendering that document, but I would let you know if we have the English translation. No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You are not tendering it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it there are no objections from the Defence in relation to all the other associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So all the others will be admitted and given a number in due course by the Court Deputy. Thank you. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will try to go into private session as little as possible. That is why I will ask questions without a person mentioned. But if you see that we should go into private session, do say so. In Vogosca, there were a total of 23 police officers; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many Serbs were there among them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven were Bosniaks, one was a Croat, and all others were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have another armed formation at your disposal, apart from these men?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, until the reserve police force was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When was that force established?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the 20th of September, 1991. It was on the 19th, the 20th, or the 21st of September. I'm not sure about the exact date, but it was on one of these three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of this additional police force, the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In percentages, it was the same as the active-duty staff; that is, 65 to 70 per cent Serbs, about 25 per cent Bosniaks, and about 5 per cent Croats. And there were also some Yugoslav people who declared themselves as Yugoslavs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, then, Witness, I put it to you that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, led by the SDA and its representatives and the authorities, especially in the police, there was urgent activity to establish an army clandestinely, and it was supposed to consist of the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, the Territorial Defence and the Muslim members of the police. What do you say to that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a total lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now see where it started in the police. You described the structure of the MUP of the republic; correct? Tell us who the minister of the interior was.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, that's no problem. It was Alija Delimustafic. His deputy was Vitomir Zepinic. Alija Delimustafic was appointed by the SDA and Zepinic by the SDS. You appointed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let's proceed by the five administrations that you have described and that you know. Who was the chief and who was a deputy; that is, the number-one man and the number-two man?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. The chief of the Police Administration was Avdo Hebib. Are you listening to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the head of the Police Administration, the uniformed police, was Avdo Hebib, and his deputy was Slavko Draskovic, also known as Kudro, a well-known SDS member. I'm sure you know him well. The chief of the Crime Prevention Department was Momcilo Mandic. That was the police that worked on crime in plain clothes. And his deputy was Hasib Dizdarevic. The minister's assistant for communications was Akif Sabic. I don't know who the chief was. The assistant minister for financial and materiel was Bruno Stojic, and he later became the first minister of the MUP of the so-called Herceg-Bosna. And then there was also the personnel administration. The assistant for personnel was Hilmo Selimovic. These are well-known facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the number two in that administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he's a Muslim. Only God can know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we have a redaction at line 17, 17/18?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I don't see why lines 17 and 18 should be redacted. There's nothing that can serve to identify this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, who was the deputy chief of communications?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the level of the republic, there was an inter-party agreement to share power in such a way that the number-one man in one service or administration would be of one ethnicity and the number-two man from another ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. This principle is even now applied in the institutions of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the reason why Bosnia doesn't have a government today and that the Croats are complaining that they have been deceived?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know why the Croats are complaining. Have you to ask them. But you co-operated quite well with them at the time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the minister was a Muslim. The head of communications and the technical service that did the wire-tapping was a Muslim. His deputy, in any case, was not a Serb. The head of the Police Administration was a Muslim; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you said something that was incorrect. That is not correct. The Communications Sector, headed by Akif Sabic, a Bosniak Muslim, did not carry out the wire-tapping that you are talking about. This is the Public Security Service. The wire-taping was conducted by the State Security Service. These are two different sections and have nothing to do with each other. It's a fact that the minister was a Muslim Bosniak. His deputy was a Serb. It's true that the head of Communications was a Bosniak. I said that I don't know who his deputy was. I don't know if it was a Serb or not. I wasn't really too interested in that. The fact is that the head of the uniformed police was a Bosniak, but the fact is also that the number-two man in that structure was a Serb, Slavko Draskovic, Kudro. I already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the head of personnel was Hilmo Selimovic, and his deputy was a Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Draskovic, Mandic, did any of those people that you are calling the cadres of the SDS were a member of the SDS when they came to the police for the first time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when they came to the police. I wasn't interested either. But I know that they were members of the Serbian Democratic Party, because -- just let me finish -- because on two or three occasions they organised press conferences conducted by Slavko Draskovic, or Mandic at one point, because they complained that as members of the Serbian Democratic Party in the Ministry of Internal Affairs, they were discriminated against. These were public press conferences that anybody could follow. So they, themselves, declared themselves as members of the Serbian Democratic Party. You cannot claim that they were not members of the SDS and that you did not appoint them to those positions as representatives of the Serbs from the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, they held a press conference to say that members of the Serbian people were deceived, over-voted, and replaced, not members of the Serbian Democratic Party, and we have enough evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are not going to debate this.

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we're not going to debate this. I just want to say this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how it was in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, both Dr. Karadzic and the witness, with respect, need to be reminded, I think, to have some pauses between their questions and answers and to not argue with one another, because this becomes impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just slow down and put a pause between the question and answer. We have to follow. Yes, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I will try to slow down. But please allow me to answer the question. The first high-ranking official in the MUP who was replaced was a Bosniak. His name was Osman Jasarevic. And it's not true that the Serbs were replaced, manipulated, and all of that. These assertions absolutely do not stand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must apologise to the Trial Chamber and to the OTP, to Madam Edgerton, but this witness is resorting to generalised statements, to which I have to respond. However, let's stick to what you know, Witness, sir. Can we now move into private session, because we are going to be dealing with your municipality now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have anything to say before we go into private session, Mr. Witness? Yes, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not resorting to any generalised statements. I stand behind everything that I am saying. I don't want my testimony to be understood as any kind of argument or quarrelling. I stated solemnly that I would speak the truth and nothing but the truth, and I will not be saying anything other than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Who was appointed instead of Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kemal Sabovic was appointed in his stead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is his ethnicity? Is he the same as Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Since he became deputy minister of the MUP in Bosnia and Herzegovina, a deputy of Bruno Stojic, he is a Bosniak, but in the para-state of Herceg-Bosna he was at the post of deputy minister for internal affairs. And you probably know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When Sabovic was replaced, who came in his place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bakir Osmanagic came in his stead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosniak. I don't know why that is controversial, that all of them are Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is not controversial. The post belonged to Bosniaks, so when one was replaced, he was replaced by another Bosniak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be logical. According to the inter-party agreement, it would be logical for things to proceed like that. But you are deliberately not stating one fact, and that is that the chief of the Security Services Centre had assistants who were Serbs, Croats, Yugoslavs and so on and so forth. And another fact you are just ignoring and that is that the structure of the employees in the republican MUP, in the CSBs, and in other security service centres, was quite unfavorable for the Bosniaks and for Croats, because the Serbs made up an overwhelming majority in those places, and you are just not mentioning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, that is not our topic. We will be dealing with that in another way. All I'm asking you is this: Is it normal that if a certain post was given to a Muslim, that when that person was replaced, it would be given to another Muslim? I mean, a Serb could be placed to that post, but that post still belonged to the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the inter-party agreement, that post belonged to the SDA, so it would be logical that a Muslim would be appointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Still --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Still too quick in responding. Put a pause between question and answer. Shall we go into private session now? Mr. Karadzic, shall we go into private session? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has that already happened? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that Biljana Plavsic was chairman of the National Defence Council of the republic, and that it was on her orders or with her support that Alija Delimustafic, on the 21st of September, 1991, mobilised the entire reserve police force. If I put it to you that Alija Izetbegovic was chairman of the National Defence Council, and that Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic did not take part in this at all, what are you going to say to that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not going to believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're not going to believe me that Izetbegovic was chairman of the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Maybe Izetbegovic was chairman of the council, but I believe with 100 per cent certainty that it was Biljana Plavsic. And it is certain that the decision on the mobilisation of the reserve police force could not have been made without the participation of the Serb officials, that is to say, Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic. Such a major decision could not have been reached without the two of them, and you know that full well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at paragraph 46: [In English] "This entire reserve staff was mobilised pursuant to the order of Delimustafic on 21st of September, 1991." [Interpretation] Do you remember, Witness, that on 4 April, Mr. Izetbegovic mobilised the entire Territorial Defence? He ordered a general mobilisation, contrary to the demands of Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic; they were against it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from this mobilisation of the reserve forces, simultaneously Mr. Mile Hasanovic, the president of the municipality of Vogosca, simultaneously wanted to mobilise the Territorial Defence? That was in September 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us against whom the president of Vogosca municipality wanted to mobilise the Territorial Defence in September 1991? Who was the supposed enemy?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The existence of a supposed enemy was not required for the mobilisation of the Territorial Defence. The situation in the municipality was already such that the existing police forces were unable to keep law and order, and it was necessary to mobilise the Territorial Defence so that they could assist in improving the security situation in the municipality. So there was no supposed enemy as a reason for mobilisation of the Territorial Defence, since the Territorial Defence was a common force, or at least on paper, because you had already taken action, and in September 1991 you had already established your own Serb Territorial Defence at Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is wrong, sir, but I'm not -- you're not going to trap me with that. You have no proof for that. Could we please see paragraph 52 of the statement. Are you trying to say that the Territorial Defence was supposed to do policing tasks according to what law, under what law?

utterances.speaker: KDZ020 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're putting things wrong again, as if you knew what I wanted to say. Mobilising the Territorial Defence had its legal foundation in the Law on All People's Defence, and you cannot deny that. Under that law, in certain situations, when the security situation is -- has deteriorated, the Territorial Defence can be mobilised legally. But, of course, the Territorial Defence comprised of Serbs, Bosniaks, and Croats, and everybody else. But I'm not trying to trap you. My claim that you had organised the Serb Territorial Defence is completely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If it is, the Prosecution will lead evidence to that effect.
